name: Visibility of System Status
description: Interfaces should keep users informed about what the system is doing, especially after an action or during waiting. Visible status reduces guessing and makes latency or background work feel accountable.
design_relevance_note: Applies to loading states, progress bars, optimistic updates, sync indicators, save confirmations, disabled/button states, and background-job messaging.
myth_risk_note: Status visibility is logically sound and supported by the narrow existing progress-indicator finding, but the broader Nielsen heuristic lacks peer-reviewed experimental validation as a discrete design law -- treated as foundational in practice but remains more of an informed principle than a validated empirical finding.
prevalence_note: Nielsen heuristic #1 and standard UX-review vocabulary; loading/feedback/status visibility is a baseline design-review check across digital products.

findings.description: In a formal experiment with computer search tasks (48 participants), 86% of users preferred interfaces with percent-done progress indicators over those without, and rated them as more attractive/effective — even though the indicator did not reduce actual task completion time. This foundational, widely-cited finding (190 citations) underpins the modern design practice of showing immediate visual feedback/progress state, and has not been seriously disputed in the HCI literature since.
findings.source_title: The importance of percent-done progress indicators for computer-human interfaces
findings.source_venue: ACM SIGCHI Bulletin (Proceedings of the SIGCHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems, CHI '85)

applications.title: Amazon Echo's light ring indicating listening/processing state
applications.description: Amazon Echo devices use a colored light ring to show when the device is actively listening or processing a command -- a persistent, ambient signal of the system's current internal state, with no persuasion or engagement angle at all.
applications.ethical_note: A pure device-state communication signal with no persuasive or commercial angle at all -- as clean an illustration of this heuristic as exists in this corpus, useful as a contrast against entries elsewhere where a similar 'inform the user' framing is used to create urgency instead.

applications.title: Loft.com keeping out-of-stock wishlist items visible with clear status messaging
applications.description: Loft.com keeps an item on a user's wishlist even after it sells out, rather than silently removing it, and shows messaging explaining its unavailability -- preserving the user's own record while clearly communicating the system's actual state.
applications.ethical_note: Informative rather than persuasive -- this preserves the user's own record and tells the truth about availability, the opposite of a pattern that would hide or obscure a state change to keep a user engaged. A clean, low-risk illustration.
